title: How an Anthropic designer uses Claude Slides
format_note: Employee-presenter walkthrough: on-camera designer voiceover over redrawn illustrated UI, then real product capture of one workflow from voice memo to shared deck.
one_thing: You can talk through an idea on a walk, hand the transcript to Claude, and get a deck you steer with comments.

transcript.voice_style: Casual first-person designer, self-deprecating ('yap into the mic', 'it's usually a mess'), conversational pace with no sales language.
transcript.script_shape: Pain (blank window, 0:09), alternative (walk, 0:16), intro (0:20), voice memo (0:29), prompt (0:54), result and edits (1:00-1:15), share (1:20), sign-off line (1:35).

structure.frame0: Title card poster: terracotta slide on a pink-beige ground with 'How an Anthropic designer uses Claude Slides' under an active text-edit toolbar, selection on 'Claude Slides' (f0001.jpg).
structure.first_3s: Cursor selects 'Claude Slides' and the toolbar bolds it by t=2 (f0002.jpg); the card then slides left to reveal an illustrated desktop room at t=3.7 (window-04-2.959s.jpg). No speech until 5 s.

beats.what: Title card edited live: bold applied to 'Claude Slides' with a drawn cursor and toolbar.
Illustrated desktop-as-room; cursor creates 'extremely interesting idea.txt'; the blank-window problem is shown, not named.
Blank slide in a drawn slide editor; typed 'My ideaaaa / The big one / Here it comes!' as procrastination gag.
nate.png dragged onto 'The Great Outdoors' folder cuts to the live-action presenter with an editable name card.
Illustrated phone records a voice memo while the presenter walks outside in a vertical clip; typed captions on the right.
Real Voice Memos transcript dragged into Claude; prompt typed ('turn my exact words into a presentation').
Generated deck opens; subtitle italicised, a word fixed, comment sent to Claude via @Claude.
Share panel: access changed to 'Anyone at Today's Thing', Copy link.
Illustrated files (nate.png, foot pngs, breeze.wav) shuffle as a closing gag.
'Claude makes it. You steer it.' then starburst, then Claude wordmark.

hero_moment.what: Hard cut (change 93.7) from chat into the generated black deck: 'You should be able to email Claude.' The product's output is finally on screen.

ending.cta_text: Claude makes it. You steer it.
ending.what: Sign-off line edited on screen with a selection highlight, a lone starburst, then the wordmark; audio is silent from 102.14 s.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: Short opening shots (3.25 s median), one 24.96 s shot (28.6-53.6 s, 24% of runtime) held by voiceover with captions and a waveform changing every 2 s, then a six-cut run from 63 to 76 s. No burst detected.

look.ground: Warm pink-beige (f0001.jpg), swapped for sage green during the phone section (f0014.jpg); real UI sections are off-white.
look.accent_use: Terracotta is the dominant block colour (title card, record widget, async slide); lavender marks name card and caption boxes. Bold is the only emphasis in the title.
look.type: Serif display (Anthropic Serif style) for titles and clock; sans for UI labels, file names and prompt. Small tracked uppercase terracotta kicker above slide titles ('HERE'S MY IDEA').

motion.eases: Not measured from motion curves. Strip frames show a quick decelerating slide for the title card exit and linear typing cadence.

copy.holds_vs_reading_rule: Titles hold past 0.5 s + 0.3 s a word (7 words needs 2.6 s, gets 3.7 s). The 30-word prompt needs 9.5 s, typed over 6 s. The sign-off holds 2 s against 2.3 s needed.

sound.music: Audio kind is music with speech (describe: speech 0.701, music 0.583); no steady beat (confidence 0.092), no bpm. Eight sections A-H. No instrument named; keyboard_musical 0.26 is the top music tag.
sound.sfx: Describe tags click 0.248 and typing 0.224 suggest interface sounds under the typing and click beats. Not heard; inferred from tags.
sound.vo_music_balance: Presenter speech dominates; whole film is quiet at -25.7 LUFS integrated, short-term max -20.8, true peak -3.9 dBTP, LRA 8.8 LU.
sound.energy_arc: Flat and conversational; no louder section is identified. Silence from 102.14 s to the end (2.0 s) under the logo.
sound.sync_to_picture: cuts_on_strong_onset_share 0.40 against chance 0.121: cuts lean on sound onsets, but onsets are mostly speech and typing, not musical beats.

good.observation: The title card is itself an edit: select 'Claude Slides', toolbar appears, bold lands by t=2. The film demonstrates the product in its first frame with no logo.
Pain is shown, not named: a blank slide and a typed 'My ideaaaa' gag cover 'staring at a blank window' before the narrator says it.
Product UI is cropped to the one thing to read: prompt box, slide title, share dialog each fill most of the frame at the moment they matter.
Every overlay is drawn as an editable object of the product, such as the name card with handles and the caption box, so graphics and subject share one visual language.
A closed loop for the user: voice memo, transcript, prompt, deck, comment, share. Each step is a distinct visible screen, so the whole workflow reaches the screen.
Ending is a three-step build with a silent last two seconds: sentence with selection highlight, lone starburst, wordmark.
good.evidence: f0049.jpg, f0050.jpg, f0051.jpg, f0052.jpg; audio silence_spans 102.14-104.13

weak.observation: Dense real-UI shot of the Voice Memos window over Claude is unreadable at phone width, and it carries the proof that the transcript is the user's own words.
Caption box stops at 'it's just for' and collapses before the voiceover finishes 'me and Claude', so the text and speech end out of step.
Loudness is far below the social target: -25.7 LUFS integrated would play quietly beside feed content.
No burst of cuts or musical hit supports the hero reveal; it arrives as one hard cut into a static deck.

rule_candidates.rule: Open with the product doing a visible edit to the title itself (select, toolbar, bold) instead of a logo; make the hook an action reviewable in frames 0-2 s.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0001.jpg to f0002.jpg, window-01-0.25s.jpg: selection and bold within 0.4 s.

rule_candidates.rule: Keep titles at 6-8.5% of frame height with one bold accent phrase and at most 5 words per line.
rule_candidates.evidence: title_measurements: 61.5 px (8.5%) at t=2; 43-44 px (6%) at t=64.

rule_candidates.rule: A voice-led story may hold one composition up to 25 s if some element changes at least every 2 s (caption growth, waveform, new clip) and shot median across the film stays near 3 s.
rule_candidates.evidence: 28.6-53.6 s shot (24% of runtime); window-24-27.042s.jpg; median_shot_s 3.25.

rule_candidates.rule: Show the output of the product at 55-65% of runtime with one hard cut into a full-frame result, and let the preceding 60 s build the question it answers.
rule_candidates.evidence: hero cut at 63.17 s, share 0.607; f0033.jpg.

rule_candidates.rule: Do not force a burst of 5-8 cuts in 5 s on a calm explainer; six cuts spread over about 12 s from 63 to 76 s were enough here.
Where real UI follows illustration, crop the capture so the text that matters reaches 2.6% of frame height or more; whole-window shots belong only to orientation.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0028.jpg text about 1.5% vs f0030.jpg prompt text about 3.2%.

rule_candidates.rule: Draw lower thirds and captions as editable objects of the product (handles, toolbar) that settle to clean text within 1-2 s, so graphics belong to the film's world.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0011.jpg handles and toolbar, f0012.jpg clean card; window-24-27.042s.jpg holds clean.

rule_candidates.rule: Presenter-led brand films may sit near -25 LUFS with -4 dBTP; apply the -14 LUFS social master only when a feed spot is the destination.
